designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: As someone with an old car, I'd laugh out loud at this. Anyone who drives gets the joke in two seconds, and the clean icon grid looks smart, not like a gag tee. The tiny labels can't be read from across a room, but you don't need them; they're a bonus up close.
designs.fix: Make PROBABLY FINE. bigger, about the full width of the icon grid, so the punchline reads from across a parking lot and not just the icons.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: This is exactly my dog. The brushy drawings are charming and have personality, the 'Turn around.' repeats are a perfect slow-burn joke, and '7. Sigh.' made me smile. It looks like nice illustration, not a meme. The light serif captions get thin and small on the shirt, so you have to stand close.
designs.fix: Make the captions heavier and a bit bigger (and the title too) so 'Turn around.' x4 reads at conversation distance, especially in white ink on the black tee.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Every cat owner has lived this exact story, and the three panels tell it with no words needed. The smug, eyes-closed cat in panel 3 is the payoff and it's drawn really well. Clean, bold line work that looks good on either color. It's a bit tall and narrow on the back, and the cat detail gets small from a distance.
designs.fix: Draw the panels bigger (wider print area) so the cat's smug face in panel 3 reads from a few meters away, since that face is the whole punchline.
